title: The SEC Suspected a Ponzi Scheme in 1997. Allen Stanford Kept Selling Until 2009
summary: 1997: SEC examiners in Fort Worth write "Possible misrepresentations. Possible Ponzi scheme." about Allen Stanford's offshore bank. It kept selling certificates of deposit until February 2009. Built from the SEC's complaint, the order appointing a receiver, the government's appellate brief, the U.S. Attorney's releases, the SEC inspector general's report and the Fifth Circuit's ruling, this is the paper trail: the fake profits, the auditor and the regulator who were paid, the $541 million capital infusion that wasn't, the 13 guilty verdicts and the 110-year sentence — and what happened after.
